T0604.title: Proxy Pool, Residential Proxy, Datacenter Proxy
T0604.definition: The classification of proxy IP resources by source and form: residential proxies (real home-broadband IPs), datacenter proxies (datacenter IPs), and tunneling proxies (dynamic forwarding).
T0604.description: Proxy IP resources are mainly classified into three types by source and form: residential proxies originate from IPs assigned by real home-broadband ISPs, belong to real carriers and geographies, carry high reputation and are the hardest for proxy detection (A0038) to block, making them the first choice for black-market scraping and credential stuffing — and the most expensive. Datacenter proxies originate from cloud datacenters and IDCs — cheap, highly concurrent, and low-latency, but their IP ranges clearly belong to datacenters, making them easy for IP intelligence (A0016-001) and proxy detection to flag. Tunneling proxies achieve single-ingress dynamic forwarding to a large number of egress IPs, enabling single-access-point IP rotation, balancing usability and IP volume. The three types are commonly integrated into a proxy pool (AT0098) for on-demand scheduling, and together with IP providers (TA0011) form the black-market IP supply chain, used to evade IP rate limiting, blocklists, and geo-fencing.
T0604.usageExample: A scraping gang rents a residential proxy pool to evade IP rate limiting, keeping each egress IP's request frequency below the threshold to bypass cloud anti-scraping.
